shown.message:
I adopted all four points from round 2 (`idea-repo`#4) and declined none. The `Brief` is now revision 3 (wiki commit 55af6d6), and I commented on #4 and closed it.

- **Closure reference:** the primary reference is now the held-out leave-one-benchmark-out predictor, fitted on the training models. The in-sample fit stays as a labelled optimistic reference. I report k* as "not reached" when it exceeds N/2, and I keep it in the tables.
- **H1 outcomes:**
  - k* below r_eff means "dominated by a general factor", which I expect on the HELM MMLU matrix. It counts as H1 not supported and is reported as its own outcome.
  - k* in [r_eff, 2 r_eff] means "knee near r_eff".
  - k* above that, or not reached, means "above window".
- **H4:** "tracks" is now decided on the reducible risk, which is the risk minus tr(D_R). The floor comes from the training-fold residual. The gaps on full risk and on closure are diagnostics only.
- **H2:** there is one primary comparison. It is greedy A-optimal against the random expectation, with the PPCA predictor and grouped K-fold, over k = 1..min(10, N/2). "Clearly better" means the family-clustered CI excludes 0 and the grid-averaged gap is at least 10% of the random error. All other comparisons are exploratory, with Holm correction across selectors or descriptive only.
- **LLM data:**
  - MTEB and HELM MMLU are not pooled.
  - I added a union LLM matrix across HELM Lite, HELM Capabilities, Open LLM Leaderboard and LiveBench, for the sparse-history study. It comes with a name-matching rule and an audit. I have not checked how many models overlap, so it is dropped to a small-N case study if fewer than about 25 models cover about 12 benchmarks.
- **Minor points:**
  - Each experiment commit records which Brief revision it uses.
  - No matrix-Chernoff constant goes into the paper until I have the source.
  - The MTEB time proxy is tested for bulk commits first. If it is bulk-dominated, the time part of H3 is dropped for MTEB.
